```{r}
library(readr)
library(bio3d)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
pdb_stats <- as.data.frame(read_csv("pdb_stats.csv"))
cols_to_pivot <- colnames(pdb_stats)[2:8]   

```
> Q1: What percentage of structures in the PDB are solved by X-Ray and Electron Microscopy.

`r sum(pdb_stats$X_ray) / sum(pdb_stats$Total)`

> Q2: What proportion of structures in the PDB are protein?

`r sum(pdb_stats[1:3,9]) / sum(pdb_stats$Total)`

> Q3: Type HIV in the PDB website search box on the home page and determine how many HIV-1 protease structures are in the current PDB?

513

![1HSG](1HSG.png)

```{r}
pdb_long <- pivot_longer(pdb_stats, cols=cols_to_pivot, names_to="category", values_to = "count")
ggplot(pdb_long) +
  aes(x=reorder(Molecular_Type, -count, sum),y=count,fill=category) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity",position="stack")
```

> Q4: Water molecules normally have 3 atoms. Why do we see just one atom per water molecule in this structure?

To reduce visual clutter. Molstar defaults to showing the oxygen atom only.

> Q5: There is a critical “conserved” water molecule in the binding site. Can you identify this water molecule? What residue number does this water molecule have

residue 308

```{r}
hsg <- read.pdb("1hsg")
hsg
```
> Q7: How many amino acid residues are there in this pdb object?

`r length(pdbseq(hsg))`

> Q8: Name one of the two non-protein residues?

Nucleic atoms

> Q9: How many protein chains are in this structure?

2

```{r}
adk <- read.pdb("6s36")
m <- nma(adk)
mktrj(m, file="adk_m7.pdb")
plot(m)
```

> Q10. Which of the packages above is found only on BioConductor and not CRAN?

BiocManager

> Q11. Which of the above packages is not found on BioConductor or CRAN?

"Grantlab/bio3d-view"

>  True or False? Functions from the devtools package can be used to install packages from GitHub and BitBucket?

True

```{r}
id <- "1ake_A"
aa <- get.seq(id)
```

```{r, cache=True}
blast <- blast.pdb(aa)
hits <- plot(blast)
```

```{r, cache=True}
fiels <- get.pdb(hits$pdb.id, path="pdbs", split=TRUE)
```


```{r}
pdbs <- pdbaln(fiels, fit=TRUE, exefile="msa")
```






```{r}
files <- get.pdb(hits$pdb.id, path="pdbs", split=TRUE, gzip=TRUE)
pdbs <- pdbaln(files, fit = TRUE, exefile="msa")
ids <- basename.pdb(pdbs$id)
plot(pdbs, labels=ids)
```
